source_caption:
🎬 Same Kind of Different as Me (2017)

Same Kind of Different as Me tells the inspiring true story of Ron Hall, a successful international art dealer whose comfortable life begins to change when his wife Deborah encourages him to volunteer at a homeless shelter in Fort Worth, Texas. While struggling to repair their troubled marriage, Ron reluctantly agrees to help, eventually meeting Denver Moore, a homeless man with a painful past who initially wants nothing to do with him. Despite their completely different backgrounds, Deborah believes that Denver will play an important role in their lives. As Ron gradually earns Denver’s trust, an unexpected friendship develops, transforming their understanding of compassion, forgiveness, faith, and the importance of helping others. When the family faces a heartbreaking challenge, their bond becomes a powerful source of strength and hope. Starring Greg Kinnear, Renée Zellweger, Djimon Hounsou, and Jon Voight, the film delivers an emotional and uplifting story about friendship, redemption, kindness, and the extraordinary ways people can change one another’s lives.

🎭 Genre: Biography • Drama • Faith-Based

⭐ IMDb: 6.6/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 59m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Michael Carney

✍️ Writers: Michael Carney, Alexander Foard & Ron Hall

📚 Based On: The bestselling memoir Same Kind of Different as Me by Ron Hall, Denver Moore, and Lynn Vincent.

📺 Where to Watch: Check Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV for current streaming or rental availability in the United States.

source_details.synopsis: Same Kind of Different as Me is a 2017 American Christian drama film directed by Michael Carney, in his feature directorial debut, and written by Ron Hall, Alexander Foard and Michael Carney. It is based on the 2006 book by Hall, Denver Moore and Lynn Vincent. The film stars Greg Kinnear, Renée Zellweger, Djimon Hounsou, Olivia Holt, Jon Voight, and Stephanie Leigh Schlund. The film was released on October 20, 2017, by Pure Flix Entertainment. The film received mixed reviews but still made $6.4 million in cinemas against a total budget of $6.5 million including marketing and advertising.
